title: Data Log 1: Creating lists
lessonSummary: Great! You created lists and measured their length.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: An empty list, a text list and a number list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
leer = []
modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield", "Radar", "Radio"]
zahlen = [1, 5, 10, 15, 20]
print(f"Empty: {leer}")
print(f"List: {modules}")
print(f"Numbers: {zahlen}")
print(f"Count: {len(modules)}")

tasks.instruction: Create a list modules with the five texts Drive, Sensor, Shield, Radar and Radio (in this order). Then print exactly Count: 5 by using len().
Create an empty list called empty. Then print Empty: [] (put the list into the text) and on the next line Length: 0 (with len()).

title: Data Log 2: Accessing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You access entries by index and can change them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: First and last entry and a list inside a list.
tasks.codeTemplate:
modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield", "Radar", "Radio"]
print(f"First: {modules[0]}")
print(f"Last: {modules[-1]}")
party = [["Nova", "Pilot", 15], ["Kira", "Technician", 12]]
print(f"Name of the second: {party[1][0]}")

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Print the second entry as Second: Sensor and the second to last as Second to last: Radar (using the indices 1 and -2).

validation.expected:
Second: Sensor
Second to last: Radar

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Replace the first entry with Core and print the list with print(). It must then look like this: ['Core', 'Sensor', 'Shield', 'Radar', 'Radio']
The list modules is provided. Print the first three entries with a slice [0:3] and on the next line the last two with [-2:]: ['Drive', 'Sensor', 'Shield'] and ['Radar', 'Radio']

title: Data Log 3: Adding entries
lessonSummary: Great! Your lists grow with append() and insert().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: append, insert and joining two lists with +.
tasks.codeTemplate:
modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield"]
modules.append("Laser")
modules.insert(0, "Core")
print(modules)
mehr = modules + ["Scanner"]
print(f"Joined: {mehr}")

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Use append() to add Laser and then Scanner and print the list. It must look like this: ['Drive', 'Sensor', 'Shield', 'Laser', 'Scanner']
The list modules is provided. Use insert() to put the entry Core at the start (index 0) and print exactly First: Core (using modules[0]).
The list modules is provided. Attach the three entries Laser, Scanner and Reactor in one go with extend() and print exactly Count: 6 (len).

title: Data Log 4: Removing entries
lessonSummary: Nice! You can remove entries on purpose.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: remove, pop and pop(0).
tasks.codeTemplate:
modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield", "Radar", "Radio"]
modules.remove("Radar")
letzter = modules.pop()
erster = modules.pop(0)
print(f"Removed: {letzter} and {erster}")
print(modules)

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Use remove() to remove the entry Radar and print the list. It must look like this: ['Drive', 'Sensor', 'Shield', 'Radio']
The list modules is provided. Take the last element out with pop() and store it in removed. Print exactly Removed: Radio and on the next line Left: 4 (len).

title: Data Log 5: Searching and counting
lessonSummary: Great! You find entries, check whether they exist and count them.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: in, index and count.
tasks.codeTemplate:
modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Drive", "Shield", "Drive", "Radar"]
print(f"Contained: {"Sensor" in modules}")
print(f"Position: {modules.index("Sensor")}")
print(f"Count: {modules.count("Drive")}")

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Check with in and print exactly Present: True for Sensor and on the next line Present: False for Laser.
The list modules (with duplicate entries) is provided. Print exactly Count Drive: 3 with count() and on the next line exactly Position Sensor: 1 with index().
The list modules (with duplicate entries) is provided. Create the list without duplicates with sorted(set(modules)) and print it: ['Drive', 'Radar', 'Sensor', 'Shield']

title: Data Log 6: Sorting
lessonSummary: Sorted! You order lists with sort(), sorted() and reverse().

tasks.instruction: Run this example: sort, sorted with reverse=True and the unchanged original.
tasks.codeTemplate:
zahlen = [5, 2, 8, 1]
kopie = sorted(zahlen, reverse=True)
print(f"Copy: {kopie}")
print(f"Original: {zahlen}")
zahlen.sort()
print(f"Sorted: {zahlen}")

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Sort it with sort() and print it. It must look like this: ['Drive', 'Radar', 'Radio', 'Sensor', 'Shield']

The list modules is provided. Create a descending copy copy with sorted(..., reverse=True). Print copy first and then modules – the original stays unchanged: ['Shield', 'Sensor', 'Radio', 'Radar', 'Drive'] and ['Drive', 'Sensor', 'Shield', 'Radar', 'Radio']
The list modules is provided. Sort it by the length of the entries with sorted(..., key=len) and print the result: ['Drive', 'Radar', 'Radio', 'Sensor', 'Shield']

title: Data Log 7: Lists and loops
lessonSummary: Great! You loop through lists with for and pass them to functions.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: for loop and enumerate.
The list values = [12, 8, 15, 5] is provided. Add all values with a for loop in the variable total (start 0) and print exactly Total: 40.

Write a function add_entry(items, entry) that attaches the entry to the list with append() (without return!). Create modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield"], call the function with Laser and print the list. It must look like this: ['Drive', 'Sensor', 'Shield', 'Laser']

title: Data Log 8: break and continue
lessonSummary: Perfect! You steer loops with break and continue.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: break ends the search, continue skips an entry.
The list modules is provided. Loop through it with for and print every entry as Check: <entry>. If the entry is Shield, then print Found! and end the loop with break.

validation.expected:
Check: Drive
Check: Sensor
Check: Shield
Found!

tasks.instruction: The list modules is provided. Print every entry as - <entry>, except Sensor: you skip that one with continue.

title: Data Log 9: List comprehension
lessonSummary: Elegant! You build lists in one go.

tasks.instruction: Run this example: transforming and filtering in one line.
tasks.codeTemplate:
schaden = [3, 7, 12, 5]
verdoppelt = [wert * 2 for wert in schaden]
grosse = [wert for wert in schaden if wert > 4]
print(f"Doubled: {verdoppelt}")
print(f"Big: {grosse}")

tasks.instruction: The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list doubled (every value times 2) with a list comprehension and print it: [6, 14, 24, 10]
The list numbers = [3, 7, 12, 5] is provided. Build the list big with a list comprehension and an if that only contains values above 4, and print it: [7, 12, 5]
The list modules is provided. Build the list loud with a list comprehension in which every entry is in capital letters via .upper(), and print it: ['DRIVE', 'SENSOR', 'SHIELD', 'RADAR', 'RADIO']

tasks.instruction: Step 1 – Check: Create modules = ["Drive", "Sensor", "Shield"]. Check with in and print exactly Sensor present: True and on the next line Laser present: False.

Laser present: False
